title: Gospel always sets faith and repentance as prior conditions of remission
source_text: VII. Unde est quod Evangelium perpetuo ponit fidem & poenitentiam, tanquam conditiones ad remissionem peccatorum praevias. Si, inquit Dominus Jesus, poenitentiam non egeritis, omnes similiter peribitis. Luc. 13. Et post eum Petrus Apostolus, Poenitemini & convertimini, ut deleantur peccata vestra. Act. 3. 19. Quibus consonat quod ait Salomo, Qui abscondit scelera sua non dirigetur, (seu non prosperabitur): Qui autem confessus fuerit, & reliquerit ea, misericordiam consequetur. Prov. 28. 13. Similiter haec sunt verba Christi. Qui credit in eum, nempe Dei Filium, non judicatur: qui autem non credit jam judicatus est, quia non credit in Nomen unigeniti Filii Dei. Joan. 3. Quibus consonat quod subdit eodem capite Joannes Baptista. Qui est incredulus Filio non videbit vitam, sed ira Dei manet super eum.
pass_a_gloss: Hence it is that the Gospel perpetually sets faith and repentance as conditions prior to the remission of sins. If, says the Lord Jesus, you do not repent, you will all likewise perish (Luke 13). And after him the Apostle Peter: Repent and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out (Acts 3:19). With which agrees what Solomon says: He who hides his crimes will not be directed (or will not prosper); but he who has confessed and forsaken them will obtain mercy (Prov. 28:13). Likewise these are Christ’s words: Whoever believes in him, namely the Son of God, is not judged; but whoever does not believe is already judged, because he does not believe in the Name of the only-begotten Son of God (John 3). With which agrees what John the Baptist adds in the same chapter: Whoever is unbelieving toward the Son will not see life, but the wrath of God remains upon him.
pass_b_english: Gospel never detaches pardon from prior faith and repentance—Luke 13; Acts 3:19; Prov. 28:13.
John 3: belief escapes judgment; unbelief already judged, wrath remaining.

choices.why: Faith and repentance precede actual remission.
